title: Beyond Marginal Risk: ESG and Multidimensional Fragility in Equity Markets
abstract: arXiv:2611.20589v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Do ESG characteristics provide financial resilience beyond conventional risk, and is that inference stable to the financial state and ESG score being measured? We study a point-in-time panel of nonfinancial S&P 500 constituents from January 2019 through November 2025. Once ex ante return, volatility, and liquidity exposures are modeled explicitly, the broad downside-resilience pattern attenuates and none of the three primary marginal ESG $\times$ Down tests survives Holm adjustment under either conventional or wild-cluster-bootstrap inference. A post-primary exact decomposition then shows that the negative Return+RVOL coefficient is almost entirely allocated to observations that also breach the CHL trading-cost tail, while the mutually exclusive Return+RVOL-only component is essentially zero.
